title: Staging primitives extension: moves, deletes, and fenced ledger append
objective: The WP-200 staging protocol supports the full transaction operation vocabulary (move, delete_generated) with the same recovery guarantees as replaces, and provides a fenced, fsynced, bounded-retry append primitive with parent-directory creation for the ADR 0010 ledger — unblocking WP-300.
business_value: WP-300 correctly blocked on these contractual gaps: the transaction engine cannot honor the schema's operation vocabulary or the ADR 0010 append sequencing without them (see the WP-300 blocker report).
scope: Extend the intent/staging model in src/workctx/adapters/filesystem/staging.py so intent targets carry an operation kind: replace (existing behavior, unchanged), move (source path + destination, preimage-preserving, atomic per ADR 0006 semantics), and delete (preimage-preserving removal); recovery inspection, completion, and rollback must cover all three kinds with the same failure-injection rigor as the existing replace tests

Add a fenced append primitive: append bytes as one durable line-oriented write to a target file under the held lock (nonce fence verified immediately before the write), fsynced, bounded-retry on Windows PermissionError, creating missing parent directories inside the context root; designed for 99_meta/audit/ledger.jsonl but path-agnostic within the boundary

The append primitive must be usable while a prepared intent for the same transaction remains active, and must not disturb intent finalize semantics (ADR 0010: ledger append happens after the replace sequence, before intent removal)

Preserve every existing public API and behavior byte-for-byte: all current tests/filesystem tests pass unmodified; intent.json remains backward-readable or its version field is bumped with a clear error for old records (document the choice)
Update docs/reference/canonical-store.md for the extended vocabulary and the append primitive
non_goals: No transaction engine logic (WP-300 composes these primitives)
No ledger format or hash-chain semantics (WP-300 owns ADR 0010 implementation)
No changes outside the filesystem adapter, its tests, and its reference doc
deliverables: Extended staging with move/delete target kinds and full recovery coverage
Fenced append primitive with parent-dir creation
acceptance_criteria: Move and delete targets apply atomically, roll back from preimages, and are reported correctly by recovery inspection after injected mid-sequence failures (per kind and mixed-kind sequences)

Fenced append: nonce mismatch aborts without writing; missing parent directories are created inside the boundary only; injected PermissionError retries then surfaces a recoverable error; appended lines are durable (fsynced) and complete (no torn lines under injected failure)
Append while a prepared intent is active works and finalize semantics are unchanged
All pre-existing tests/filesystem tests pass unmodified
Path-boundary enforcement covers move destinations and append targets (escape attempts refused)
security_constraints: Fictional fixtures only; primitives never write outside the context root
Delete preimages are retained for rollback, honoring raw-evidence retention expectations of callers
stop_conditions: Backward compatibility for existing staging consumers cannot be preserved
Any needed change to frozen files or ADR semantics
